transformations.edit: Replaced the seed string recorder with an executable Verus function for the Rust 1.96 target body.

Adapted the inherent `[T]` receiver to an explicit `slice_ref: &mut &'a [T]` parameter, named the return value for Verus, and represented the generic `R: OneSidedRange<usize>` input with a target-local `OneSidedRangeSpec` carrying the same bound-kind/index observation used by the Rust helper.

Materialized the source-backed private `split_point_of` helper and `Direction::{Front,Back}` cases in the harness, including the `StartInclusive`, `End`, and `EndInclusive` branches and the `checked_add(1)` overflow-to-None path.

Preserved the target control flow after helper desugaring: split-point None returns None, out-of-bounds split index returns None, otherwise `split_at(split_index)` feeds the `Direction::Front` and `Direction::Back` reassignment/return branches.

Added proof-only `lemma_split_at` and view equality assertions connecting `front`/`back` to the generated `slice_split_off_partition` postcondition; the executable split, reassignment, and return branches are unchanged.
